READING

**What is fixed and what varies**

The 280 extra learning-curve remakes (10 technicians × 28 remakes each) cost GBP 26,880 and are incurred under either course; they are not a variable in the decision. What varies is (a) whether GBP 44,000 of overtime is spent; (b) whether crossing remakes are incurred; (c) whether a dual shade and material library runs for nine months; and (d) the shape of the quality exposure seen by forty practices.

**Estimating the AVENSWOOD crossing-remake bill**

The pilot gives a usable baseline: 2 technicians on the new system, 10 on the old, 4 months, 40 crossing remakes. That is approximately 5 crossing remakes per technician-month of whichever side of the split is in the minority.

Under AVENSWOOD the minority side rotates:
- Phase 1 (Jan–Apr 2027): 3 new, 9 old, 3 months → minority = 3 → 5 × 3 × 3 = 45 remakes
- Phase 2 (Apr–Jul 2027): 6 new, 6 old, 3 months → minority = 6 → 5 × 6 × 3 = 90 remakes
- Phase 3 (Jul–Oct 2027): 9 new, 3 old, 3 months → minority = 3 → 5 × 3 × 3 = 45 remakes

Total: approximately 180 crossing remakes × GBP 96 = GBP 17,280.

That estimate is rough; the true number could be anywhere from GBP 12,000 to GBP 20,000 depending on how case-continuity actually distributes. But it is not GBP 44,000.

**Net financial position**

| Item | KIRKBANE | AVENSWOOD |
|---|---|---|
| Learning-curve remakes (fixed) | GBP 26,880 | GBP 26,880 |
| Overtime | GBP 44,000 | — |
| Crossing remakes | — | ~GBP 15,000 |
| **Variable total** | **GBP 44,000** | **~GBP 15,000** |

AVENSWOOD is cheaper by roughly GBP 29,000. That gap is large enough to survive a generous upward revision of the crossing-remake estimate and still favour AVENSWOOD.

**The lab-wide quality picture**

KIRKBANE puts all ten transitioning technicians on an 11.4% remake rate simultaneously. With the pilot pair still in or just past their own curve, the laboratory's overall remake rate in January 2027 is approximately:

(10 × 11.4% + 2 × ~4%) / 12 ≈ 10.2%

against a settled baseline of 3.1%. Every one of forty practices sees that jump in the same month. It is the right thing to communicate in advance, and practices will accept a one-off explanation, but the spike is real and simultaneous across the whole client base.

AVENSWOOD caps the exposure. With only 3 of 12 technicians on the steep part at any moment, the lab-wide remake rate in the worst opening month is roughly:

(3 × 11.4% + 9 × 3.1%) / 12 ≈ 5.2%

That is elevated but never catastrophic. Three-quarters of every practice's incoming work stays at settled quality throughout.

**The dual library risk**

This is AVENSWOOD's genuine weak point. Running two shade and material libraries for nine months is not merely an administrative nuisance; it is an ongoing source of shade-mismatch errors that are harder to count than remakes but are visible to practices in the fit of restorations on returning patients. The brief explicitly flags it, which suggests Sunniva already senses its weight. The mitigation is strict assignment discipline—each practice is locked to one system for the duration and never splits a case—but that adds management load.

The crossing remakes themselves are the most insidious quality risk: they happen for no clinical reason and are the hardest to explain to a practice. The estimate of ~180 crossing remakes, however, is modest relative to the total volume (roughly 7,750 units over nine months) and is a known, budgetable quantity.

**Deadline check**

Both courses complete well before the 2028-06-30 Kessendale end-of-support date. Under AVENSWOOD the last technician moves off Kessendale on 2027-10-04; their learning curve runs into mid-2028 but they are already on the new system. No deadline risk either way.

**Weighing it up**

KIRKBANE's overtime cost is certain; AVENSWOOD's crossing-remake cost is an estimate that is unlikely to exceed GBP 20,000 in any plausible scenario. The GBP 24,000–29,000 net saving from AVENSWOOD is accompanied—not offset—by a peak lab-wide remake rate roughly half that of KIRKBANE. The dual library is the price, and it is manageable with clear practice assignment rules and a single named person owning library integrity for nine months.

KIRKBANE's clean-break appeal is real, but GBP 44,000 of overtime is a large certain outlay to buy that simplicity when the alternative can be managed with process discipline.

---

READING

The fixed learning-curve cost of GBP 26,880 (ten technicians × 28 excess remakes × GBP 96) is identical under both courses. Under KIRKBANE the variable cost is GBP 44,000 in quoted overtime. Under AVENSWOOD the variable cost is approximately GBP 15,000–17,000 in crossing remakes, estimated by scaling the pilot's 40 crossing remakes over four months (5 per minority-side technician-month) across AVENSWOOD's three phases: roughly 45 + 90 + 45 = 180 remakes at GBP 96 each ≈ GBP 17,280. Net saving from AVENSWOOD: approximately GBP 27,000–29,000. Additionally, AVENSWOOD's peak lab-wide remake rate is approximately 5–6% versus KIRKBANE's approximately 10%, since only three of twelve technicians are on the 11.4% steep section at any one time. The dual shade and material library is AVENSWOOD's genuine operating risk, but it is manageable with strict practice-to-system assignment rules and does not alter the direction of the financial or quality-exposure comparison.

CALL
AVENSWOOD

GROUNDS
AVENSWOOD saves approximately GBP 27,000–29,000 in certain overtime versus estimated crossing-remake costs, and caps the lab-wide remake rate at roughly half the KIRKBANE peak, protecting practice relationships at every stage of the transition.
